classification.difficultyReason: The student must see that the case is chosen first, then two draws with replacement. A weighted sum over the two cases gives the total probability. No tree is supplied, so the student sets up the structure and combines two conditional squared probabilities.

content.prompt:
Ravi picks one of two pencil cases at random. Case 1 has 3 blue and 2 black pens. Case 2 has 2 blue and 3 black pens.
He takes a pen from the chosen case, records its colour and puts it back, then takes another pen from the same case.
Find the probability that both pens are blue.

answer.worked:
The stages are case, first pen and second pen. Each case has probability $\frac12$. Replacement keeps the pen probabilities the same for both draws.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{both blue})&=P(\text{Case 1, B, B})+P(\text{Case 2, B, B})\\P(\text{both blue})&=\frac12\times\frac35\times\frac35+\frac12\times\frac25\times\frac25\\P(\text{both blue})&=\frac{9}{50}+\frac{4}{50}\\P(\text{both blue})&=\frac{13}{50}=26\%\end{align*}$$
